sourceFacts: Misaligned eyes can provide conflicting images, and the developing visual system can suppress one eye's input.
Suppression is functional reduced use of information, not severing of an optic nerve.
prompt:
Create an entirely original medical teaching concept illustration, landscape 3:2, warm hand-painted watercolour and gouache on ivory paper, fine ink contours, restrained navy labels, muted teal, ochre and peach accents, generous whitespace. Gentle storybook warmth with the precision and legibility of an educational atlas. Use written instructions only; no image reference. Meaningful visual relationships and sparse short labels, not paragraphs in boxes. NO internal anatomy, organ/eye/ear/brain/tissue cutaways, anatomical pathways, bones, diagnostic images, fake scans, realistic lesions, photorealistic skin, glossy wet flesh or 3D tissue. Neutral symbols or fully clothed surface poses only where specified. Preserve every direction, relationship and count in the explicit structure. Title and labels exactly as requested, no additional prose. Footer 'Educational schematic'. No logo or watermark.

Title 'Strabismic amblyopia: unequal use of input'. Two abstract signal lanes from LEFT to RIGHT with no eye, head, brain, hemisphere, cortex or nerves. LEFT upper postcard contains a crisp upright toy-star icon labelled 'Aligned input'. LEFT lower postcard contains the same star with a faint offset duplicate labelled 'Conflicting input'. UPPER lane is a broad solid teal ribbon carrying a crisp star toward a plain rectangular learning tile at RIGHT labelled 'Visual learning'. LOWER lane is an ochre ribbon that becomes pale and thin as it approaches the SAME tile, with its star fading, label 'Suppression'. Both lanes reach the tile boundary; neither is cut or physically broken. Bottom 'Information model • not nerve anatomy'. Do not put organs inside or on learning tile; only a neutral small book symbol.
